response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share_of_total, cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_count FROM c

assumptions.assumption: player_id is unique in player, so the inner join does not duplicate appearance records. Each row of appearances counts as one appearance record.
Players whose bats value is NULL or blank form their own group. That group counts toward the total and toward the average per batting hand.

alternatives.interpretation: Exclude players with an unknown (NULL) batting hand. Only real batting hands are grouped, so the total and the average cover those hands only.
alternatives.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT p.bats, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM appearances a JOIN player p ON a.player_id = p.player_id WHERE p.bats IS NOT NULL GROUP BY p.bats) SELECT bats, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share_of_total, cnt * 1.0 / AVG(cnt * 1.0) OVER () AS ratio_to_avg_count FROM c
